entries.proposition: Genre: a narrative review of MeCP2 loss (Rett syndrome), hypoxia, oxidative stress and mitochondria; search is Google Scholar to June 2025 with a term list and an English-only rule, with no counts or appraisal. WWOX is not named.
entries.snippet: A literature search was conducted on Google Scholar for peer-reviewed studies published up until June 2025.

entries.proposition: Breathing abnormalities in female patients are said to occur awake and not asleep, which bears on any nocturnal-support rationale.
entries.snippet: Breathing defects in female RTT patients result from brain stem neuronal circuit defects and are generally present during awake periods but not during sleep

entries.proposition: Hypoxaemia in patients: some measurements show a partial pressure of oxygen as low as 50 mmHg in about half of patients.
entries.snippet: with some measurements showing a partial pressure of oxygen as low as 50 mm Hg in about half of RTT patients [14]

entries.proposition: The review itself notes hyperventilation in patients occurs independently of hypoxaemia, which sits against the framing of breath-holding as the source of the hypoxia.
entries.snippet: hyperventilation appears to occur independently of hypoxemia in RTT patients [34]

entries.proposition: The MeCP2-BDNF-hypoxia mechanism is stated to be speculative and the direct mechanistic link is called under-researched.
entries.snippet: Therefore, although speculative, these results suggest that MeCP2-PARP1 interactions are involved in the resolution stage that result from adaptation to hypoxia.

entries.proposition: An unproven hypothesis is stated for breath holds as a failed BDNF-raising stimulus.
entries.snippet: One unproven hypothesis is that breath holds, which induce intermittent hypoxia, may be a way that the body attempts but fails to increase BDNF levels in RTT patients.

entries.proposition: Evidence for impaired hypoxic BDNF response: acute intermittent hypoxia raised BDNF in wild-type but not Mecp2-null male mice.
entries.snippet: acute intermittent hypoxia led to increased BDNF protein levels in wild-type Mecp2+/y, but not MeCP2-/y mice

entries.proposition: The review concedes that whether oxidative stress follows hypoxia directly, intermittent hypoxia or mitochondrial dysfunction is unresolved.
Table 1 shows tissue-dependent direction for glutathione: higher in plasma and erythrocytes with a lower ratio, lower in fibroblasts.
entries.snippet: NPBI ↑, F2-IsoPs ↑, GSH ↑, GSSG ↑, GSH:GSSG ratio ↓

entries.proposition: Same table, skin fibroblasts: GSH lower with GSSG higher.
entries.snippet: Total F2-IsoPs ↑, total F4-NeuroPs ↑, 4-HNE protein adducts ↑, NPBI ↑, GSH ↓, GSSG ↑, GSH:GSSG ratio ↓

entries.proposition: The review's own list of gaps includes that it is unclear whether recurrent hypoxia is cause or consequence of autonomic network dysregulation, and calls for long-term chronic hypoxia studies in mutant neurons.
entries.snippet: it is currently unclear whether recurrent hypoxia due to irregular breathing in RTT is a cause or consequence of CAN dysregulation

entries.proposition: Competing interest: three authors co-found 2C Bioscience.
entries.snippet: Osman Sharifi, Dag Yasui, and Janine LaSalle are co-founders of 2C Bioscience Inc.

entries.proposition: Figure 1 (colour and greyscale versions opened): three-panel scheme of hypoxia response, resolution and adaptation in which ROS drive PARP, PARP modifies HIF-1 alpha (response) or MeCP2 (resolution) and BDNF transcription is activated or repressed; it carries no data and the legend itself labels it as a proposed model.
